title: Canonical single-complex stalkwise base-change comparison in K-flat coordinates
statement: Let X', X, S', S be schemes and let f:X\to S, f':X'\to S', g:S'\to S, g':X'\to X form a cartesian square [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-base-change]. For K\in D(\mathcal O_X), K'\in D(\mathcal O_{X'}) [def-pc-derived-category] and \phi:L(g')^*K\to K' [def-pc-derived-pullback], define its canonical stalkwise comparison at z\in X' and i\in\mathbf Z. Put x=g'(z), s'=f'(z), s=f(x)=g(s'), R=\mathcal O_{S,s}, A=\mathcal O_{X,x}, B=\mathcal O_{S',s'}, C=\mathcal O_{X',z}. The R-actions on A and B and the unique map A\otimes_R B\to C are the actual scheme stalk maps, transporting B's action along the square. Choose a K-flat representative P of K [def-pc-kflat-complex], a representative N of K', isomorphisms e:Q(P)\cong K, e':Q(N)\cong K', and a chain map t:(g')^*P\to N [def-pc-module-pullback] whose image after the canonical left-derived counit equals \phi after e and e'. The counit is selected from the same universal construction as derived pullback composition [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition] and is invertible on P. Such coordinates exist by choosing N K-injective. Take the stalk complex P_x with the recorded stalk functor [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] and the specified localized comparison of the base-derived tensor cohomology model [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model], obtaining C\otimes_{A\otimes_R B}H^i(P_x\otimes_R^L B)\to H^i(P_x\otimes_A C). Follow it by the canonical degreewise pullback-stalk identification [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback] and H^i(t_z). This gives the map to H^i(N_z). Under e' and exactness of stalks [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact], its target identifies with H^i(K'_z); thus its invertibility is exactly invertibility of the canonical equation-bc map H^i(K_x\otimes_R^L B)\otimes_{A\otimes_R B}C\to H^i(K'_z), independently of the chosen coordinates. The single-complex stalk condition requires this map to be an isomorphism for every z and i.

proof.text: For exists_tensorMap use the compatible algebra maps of [lem-single-complex-stalk-algebra-maps] and Algebra.TensorProduct.lift; tensor extensionality and the lift formulas give both required restrictions. This proof was already present and is retained.

For exists_tensorStalkIso let a be the A-to-C restriction of tensorMap and use its already-proved restriction equality a = (g′.stalkMap z).hom. Prove the transport assertion for an arbitrary ring map a with this equality, eliminating the equality. The inverse of the natural stalk isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback], mapped to homological complexes with NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex, supplies the chain isomorphism. Its components are definitionally the displayed inverse components after the equality transport. Zero-preservation instances are pinned at the stalk-module universe.

For nonempty_coordinates first represent K by Q.objPreimage K and apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Its augmentation becomes an isomorphism under Q, and composition with objObjPreimageIso gives e. Apply [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] to Q.objPreimage K′; invert the localized augmentation and compose with objObjPreimageIso to obtain a K-injective N and e′.

The selected composition counit of [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition] is not required by that theorem’s signature to be invertible on K-flat complexes. Extract instead the K-flat-computing counit from exists_derivedPullback [def-pc-derived-pullback], identify its underived functor with tensorPullback by Functor.ext, and compare the two universal counits. Mathlib’s isLeftDerivedFunctor_iff_isIso_leftDerivedLift makes the comparison an isomorphism, while leftDerived_fac_app expresses the selected counit as its component followed by the K-flat-computing counit. Both factors are invertible.

Invert the selected counit at P and compose with Lg′(e.hom), phi, and e′.inv. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], this derived map has a preimage under Qh; quotient fullness gives a chain map t. Naturality of quotientCompQhIso converts the Qh equation to Q.map t equal to the displayed composite. Package P, N, e, e′, K-flatness, counit invertibility, and t into Coordinates; associativity and inverse cancellation prove represents.
